technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go as the primary language for implementing the Fabric channel configuration API extensions.
Leverage existing Hyperledger Fabric SDK structures such as configtx and configtxgen for parsing and generating config transactions.
Implement helper functions as reusable utilities within the existing configuration API package.
Follow existing code patterns and conventions in the Hyperledger Fabric codebase for consistency.
Use protobuf-based serialization for config transactions to ensure compatibility with Fabric internals.
Integrate new functions into the existing example tests to demonstrate usage and ensure backward compatibility.
assumptions: The development environment is already set up with Go and Hyperledger Fabric dependencies installed.
Existing unit and integration test frameworks are in place and functional.
The specification assumes familiarity with Hyperledger Fabric's internal configuration structures.
No major architectural changes are required; only additive features are being implemented.
All user stories can be implemented within the same module without cross-module dependencies.
Example tests are maintained in a single test file for simplicity.

activities.activity_description: Review all user stories, map them to existing Fabric APIs, and design the structure of new helper functions.
Create functions to retrieve application, orderer, or consortium org configuration and return a config.Organization object.
Add functionality to update application org and application group configurations by adding or removing policies.
Add functionality to update orderer org and orderer group configurations by adding or removing policies.
Add functionality to update consortium org, consortiums group, and consortium group configurations by adding or removing policies.
Create a function that adds an orderer org definition to a channel configuration and returns a config transaction.
Create a function that adds an application org definition to a channel configuration and returns a config transaction.
Create a function to retrieve existing MSP configuration for an organization without manual parsing.
Implement a function to revoke a certificate issued by an MSP and update the revocation list in the config transaction.
Update all example tests to demonstrate usage of the new helper functions across all user stories.
Perform code review, refactor for clarity and performance, and ensure adherence to coding standards.
Run unit and integration tests, debug issues, and ensure all acceptance criteria are met.
